messages.content:
Policy: Protected Health Information Handling
Definition: Restricts the input of person-identifiable data, business-sensitive information, and confidential data into AI tools, requiring careful anonymization assessments.
Policy Type: B

Candidate risks:
- 1: Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information — AI systems that memorize and leak sensitive personal data or infer private information about individuals without their consent. Unexpected or unauthorized sharing of data and information can compromise user expectation of privacy, assist identity theft, or loss of confidential intellectual property.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-036[close], ail-intellectual-property[related], ail-nonviolent-crimes[related]
- 2: Compromised personally identifiable information (Slattery et al., 2024) — The AI system may expose personally identifiable information (PII), either inadvertently or due to adversarial inputs, derived from training data, accessible data, or inferences. PII is any data that can be used to directly identify or contact a specific individual, either alone or in combination with other information.
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-risk-subdomain-2.1[close], ail-privacy[related], ail-specialized-advice[related]
- 3: Sharing IP/PI/confidential information with tools — AI agents with unrestricted access to resources or databases or tools could potentially store and share PI/IP/confidential information with other tools or agents when performing their actions. (Concern: AI agents may share privileged information with other tools/agents. The act of sharing the information may result in harm for the model owner, user, or others. The harm can vary based on the type and details of the information shared. Without adequate oversight, these privacy incidents might overwhelm company resources.)
- 4: Data usage rights restrictions — Terms of service, license compliance, or other IP issues may restrict the ability to use certain data for building models. (Concern: Laws and regulations concerning the use of data to train AI are unsettled and can vary from country to country, which creates challenges in the development of models.)
  Cross-mappings: llm032025-supply-chain[broad], nist-data-privacy[broad], nist-value-chain-and-component-integration[broad]
- 5: Compromised sensitive information (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023) — The AI system may expose personally sensitive information, either inadvertently or due to adversarial inputs, derived from training data, accessible data, or inferences. Sensitive personal data is information that, while not necessarily identifying an individual, could cause harm, discrimination, or distress to a person if exposed, including details about their health, finances, beliefs, behaviors, relationships, and private life circumstances.
  Cross-mappings: llm022025-sensitive-information-disclosure[close], ail-privacy[related], ail-suicide-and-self-harm[related]

matched_risks.justification: This risk directly addresses the policy's concern about protecting sensitive personal data and preventing its leakage or inference.
This risk specifically highlights the exposure of personally identifiable information, which is a key component of the policy's restrictions.
This risk directly relates to the policy's concern about preventing the sharing of confidential information with external tools.
